questions.question: 1. Which of the following is true about tree traversal?

answers.a: A tree can be traversed only in a linear fashion like an array
answers.b: A tree can be traversed only in breadth first order
answers.c: A tree can be traversed only in depth first order
answers.d: A tree can be traversed using both breadth first and depth first orders

explanations.a: Incorrect. Trees have hierarchical structures, and traversal methods are designed to systematically visit their nodes.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A tree can also be traversed using depth-first methods.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A tree can also be traversed using breadth-first traversal.
explanations.d: Correct. Trees can be traversed using Breadth First Traversal and Depth First Traversal. Depth-first methods for binary trees include preorder, inorder, and postorder traversal.

questions.question: 2. Which of the following is true about Breadth First Traversal?

answers.a: In Breadth First Traversal, nodes can be visited in any arbitrary order
answers.b: In Breadth First Traversal, nodes are traversed level by level
answers.c: In Breadth First Traversal, nodes are always traversed by following one branch to its deepest node
answers.d: Breadth First Traversal visits only the leaf nodes

explanations.a: Incorrect. Breadth First Traversal follows a systematic level-based order rather than an arbitrary order.
explanations.b: Correct. Breadth First Traversal, also called level-order traversal, processes nodes level by level. In a binary tree, nodes within a level are commonly processed from left to right.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Following one branch as deeply as possible describes depth-first behavior.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Breadth First Traversal visits internal nodes as well as leaf nodes.

questions.question: 3. Select the option which is TRUE.

answers.a: A traversal of a tree does not involve visiting all the nodes
answers.b: Traversing a tree means visiting each node in a specified order, covering all the nodes
answers.c: A tree traversal must stop as soon as a leaf node is encountered
answers.d: A tree can be traversed only when all nodes have two children

explanations.a: Incorrect. A complete tree traversal is intended to visit every node of the tree.
explanations.b: Correct. Tree traversal is a systematic process of visiting every node according to a specified order.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Encountering a leaf node does not mean that the complete traversal is finished.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Tree traversal can be performed on trees containing nodes with zero, one, or two children.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following is a Depth First Traversal of a binary tree?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Level-order traversal processes nodes according to their levels.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Breadth First Traversal is level-oriented rather than depth-oriented.
explanations.c: Correct. Inorder traversal is one of the standard depth-first traversals of a binary tree.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Level-by-level processing describes breadth-oriented traversal.

questions.question: 5. Which of the following is the correct order for preorder traversal?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This ordering corresponds to inorder traversal.
explanations.b: Correct. Preorder traversal visits the root, then the left subtree, and then the right subtree.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This ordering corresponds to postorder traversal.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Reversing the standard subtree order does not define preorder traversal.

questions.question: 6. Which of the following is the correct order for postorder traversal?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This ordering corresponds to preorder traversal.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This ordering corresponds to inorder traversal.
explanations.c: Correct. Postorder traversal visits the left subtree, then the right subtree, and finally the root.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This ordering does not represent the standard postorder traversal.

questions.question: 7. Which data structure is commonly used to implement Breadth First Traversal?

explanations.a: Correct. A queue provides First-In-First-Out behavior, which supports level-by-level traversal.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A stack provides Last-In-First-Out behavior and is commonly associated with depth-first traversal.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A heap is primarily used for priority-based operations rather than maintaining level-order traversal.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A binary search tree is a tree structure, not the traversal data structure used to maintain the Breadth First Traversal order.

questions.question: 8. Which statement correctly compares preorder, inorder, and postorder traversal?

answers.a: They all visit the root at exactly the same position
answers.b: They differ in the position at which the root is visited relative to its subtrees
answers.c: They can be used only for trees containing numeric values
answers.d: They are all forms of Breadth First Traversal

explanations.a: Incorrect. The position of the root differs among preorder, inorder, and postorder traversal.
explanations.b: Correct. The three traversals differ primarily in whether the root is processed before, between, or after its subtrees.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Traversal methods depend on the tree structure and do not require values to be numeric.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Preorder, inorder, and postorder are depth-first traversal methods for binary trees.

questions.question: 9. A binary tree has $n$ nodes. What is the time complexity of visiting every node exactly once during a standard tree traversal?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Visiting every node requires work that grows with the number of nodes.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A traversal visits all nodes, so its work is not limited to logarithmic growth.
explanations.c: Correct. If each of the $n$ nodes is visited once, the traversal takes $O(n)$ time.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Visiting each node once does not require a quadratic number of operations.
